# `useSpanUnusedSpanToWithSpan`

Suggests Effect.withSpan when an Effect.useSpan callback never uses its span, since useSpan does not parent inner spans

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Anti-pattern |
| Default severity | `suggestion` |
| Fixable | Yes |
| Effect versions | v3, v4 |
| Diagnostic codes | `TS377172` |
| Language Service name | `useSpanUnusedSpanToWithSpan` |
| Oxlint name | `effecttsgo/use-span-unused-span-to-with-span` |

## Preview

```ts
import { Effect } from "effect"

declare const fetchUser: (id: string) => Effect.Effect<{ name: string }>

export const getUser = (id: string) => Effect.useSpan("fetch-user", (_span) => fetchUser(id))
/**
                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ effecttsgo(use-span-unused-span-to-with-span): This `Effect.useSpan` callback never uses the span it receives. `Effect.useSpan` does not make that span the parent of spans created inside the callback, so they will not nest under it; `Effect.withSpan` does, and removes `ParentSpan` from the requirements.
*/
```
